RFDose: Deterministic and Stochastic RF-EMF Dose Calculator

RFDose-package.Rd

Calculates the daily dose of radiofrequency electromagnetic fields (RF-EMF) absorbed by the brain or the whole body, in mJ/kg/day, for each person of a cohort, from the self-reported use of wireless devices and the environment of each person. A deterministic model gives the doses (calculate_emf_doses()) and a stochastic model their uncertainty (calculate_emf_doses_stochastic()).

Deterministic dose model

calculate_emf_doses() calculates the doses of each row of the data (one person) for eight exposure sources: mobile phone calls, mobile data, cordless phone, far-field sources, WiFi router, laptop, tablet and other devices (smartwatch, VR headset, hotspot, Bluetooth headphones and portable gaming consoles). The dose of a source is its momentary SAR (mSAR, in mW/kg) times the exposure time (in s/day):

  • Near-field sources (devices used close to the body): the mSAR is the normalized SAR (nSAR, in W/kg per W of output power) times the output power of the device (in mW), including its duty cycle.

  • Far-field sources (mobile phone base stations and broadcast stations) and WiFi router: the mSAR is the nSAR (in W/kg per W/m\(^2\) of incident power density) times the power density (in mW/m\(^2\)).

Output powers, power densities and nSAR values are averaged over the networks, frequency bands, places, activities and positions of the device, weighted by their shares (see the source functions, e.g. mobilecall_dose()). The calculation uses three kinds of values:

  • Inputs: the columns of the data (durations of use, proportions, urbanicity, country, commuting time, use of 5G), as in example_data. Missing values are replaced by default values (defaultvariables.yaml).

  • Parameters: output powers, duty cycles, proportions and far-field power densities (params.yaml, or your own file with the argument params).

  • SAR values: from a SAR file (argument sar_file): GOLIAT values averaged over four phantoms by default, one phantom, or ETAIN (see available_sar_files()).

The result has one column per exposure source with its dose in mJ/kg/day for the chosen tissue (argument tissue: "brain" or "body").

Stochastic dose model

calculate_emf_doses_stochastic() estimates the uncertainty of the doses. It repeats the deterministic calculation n times (default: 1000), each time with the parameters, SAR values and inputs drawn around their values:

  • Parameters: with the distributions of params_distributions.yaml (lognormal or truncated lognormal for powers, beta for duty cycles and single proportions, Dirichlet for proportions that sum to 1), whose mean is the value of the parameter. See simulate_params().

  • SAR values: lognormal, with a relative standard deviation of 25% (argument sar_sd). SAR values from the same simulation are drawn together, and SAR values of 0 stay 0.

  • Inputs: durations, proportions, urbanicity and commuting time, with the distributions of input_distributions.yaml (truncated lognormal with a relative standard deviation of 20% for durations, beta or Dirichlet for proportions, categorical for urbanicity). Durations of 0 stay 0. See simulate_inputs(); draw_inputs = FALSE keeps the inputs fixed.

All rows are calculated with the same parameter draws, and the inputs of a row are drawn around its own values, so the doses of a row do not depend on the other rows. For each row and exposure source, and for the total dose, the result gives the deterministic dose, the mean and standard deviation of the doses of all draws, and their quantiles (default: median and 95% interval). Give a seed for reproducible results.

See also
